title: The three charts — #277 lane CO
headline: The last three components a filename can reach.

decisions.title: The {obeys_total} authored citations, and the {drops_total} rules I left out
decisions.lede: Filename join on the three data-visualisation-*-charts.md files: {n_line_file} line rules, {n_pie_file} pie rules, {n_bar_file} bar rules — {n_spec_total} in all. {obeys_total} bind and carry an authored sentence; {drops_total} do not bind and are declared drops, not silent omissions. Every drop is a rule about a different component sitting in this file: dv-line-009 and dv-line-010 are under the line file's own '## Spark charts' heading, and dv-pie-003 is the doughnut-centre rule in a file whose namesake has no centre.
options: Land all {obeys_total} as proposed, drops included. The three metas go into knowledge/components/ exactly as they sit in proposed-metas/ — one spliced span each, nothing else touched.
Review per component first — read the {obeys_total} sentences and the {drops_total} drop reasons one chart at a time, then land what survives.
decisions.why: Lane CJ read the same four files independently and reached the same three drops by the same reasoning. Two seats converging on dv-pie-003 and the two spark rules is the strongest signal this lane produced.

decisions.title: Does chart-donut share the pie file?
decisions.lede: The precedent is icon-button, which takes {icon_button_n} of the buttons spec's {ctk_buttons} rules because that spec names icon-only as one of its three structural variations. The pie file names the doughnut harder than that: its '## Types' section lists Doughnut as one of two types, dv-pie-009's normative text reads 'both pie and doughnut', and dv-pie-003 is a rule that binds the donut alone. Measured the other way: chart-donut.meta.json already cites dv-pie-009 and dv-pie-010 by id in its own antiPatterns, and chart-pie.meta.json says it was ported from the donut with the inner radius dropped to 0. There is no family edge between them in the graph — {family_edges} of {metas_total} metas carry one, and neither chart does; what does exist is chart-pie's not-with and yieldsTo pointing at chart-donut.
options: Yes — chart-donut takes the pie file as its home spec. It would take all {n_pie_file}, including dv-pie-003, which chart-pie drops. Authored in a following lane, same shape as this one.
No — chart-donut waits. The filename does not say 'donut', and admitting it on prose is a step toward the tier s276-D5 refused.

decisions.title: Where do the {dv_family} family rules in data-visualisation.md attach?
decisions.lede: They sit above all three. The corpus's answer today is nowhere: common-toolkit-foundations.md holds {ctk_foundations} rules that sit above the four components lane TO authored, and 0 of them were attached to any meta. So there is no precedent to follow, only one to set. Reading all {dv_family} against all three by eye gives {family_b_total} that bind, not {family_a_total}: {family_bar} on bar, {family_line} on line, {family_pie} on pie.
options: Attach all {dv_family} to each of the three — {family_a_total} edges. Simple, and {family_false} of them would be false with an authored-looking sentence on top.

Attach the authored subset per component — {family_b_total} edges. Each one read against that chart; dv-013 and dv-015 land on at most one, and the {family_shared} that bind all three identically are the first measurement of what a family node would carry.

Attach them to a chart family node instead — {family_family_total} edges once. Nothing can carry it today: obeys lives on component metas, role:chart-panel has the wrong membership ({role_members} members, and Chart-bullet is not one), and the family would need a new node kind, an inheritance edge type and a propagation rule — three vocabulary changes, each yours.
